primary_source.citation: David Burns, Masato Kurihara, Takamichi Sano, On derivatives of Kato's Euler system for elliptic curves
claims_bound: r is defined as rank E(Q), with r>0 assumed in the setup
Bockstein regulator and augmentation degree use wedge^r and I^(r-1)/I^r
Conjecture 1.1(i) is an order-of-vanishing containment indexed by algebraic r
Theorem 1.3 proves that containment under p>3, p-primary Sha finiteness over F and Q, large image, and local no-p-torsion conditions
Conjecture 1.1(iii) is the leading-term formula; arbitrary-rank proof is not claimed there
integrality is shown when BSD_p(E) is valid
for analytic rank one, Gross-Zagier/Kolyvagin are invoked to infer r=1

current_primary_controls.authors: Ashay Burungale, Christopher Skinner, Ye Tian, Xin Wan
current_primary_controls.accepted_scope: abstract advertises BSD p-parts/applications in analytic rank zero or one and p-converse results
current_primary_controls.rejected_use: not treated as an arbitrary analytic-rank-two bridge
not substituted for a complex analytic-rank-two -> algebraic-rank-two theorem

negative_history_preserved: R7 generalized-Kato route re-entered Selmer dimension plus transverse p-localization.
R6 plectic route had an intrinsic entry restriction.
R5 scalar/base-change theta path did not supply plectic nonvanishing.
This cycle did not repeat those theorem-cell searches.

derived_scope_result.statement: BKS's direct higher-derivative carrier is algebraic-rank-indexed. Complex analytic rank two alone does not license setting r=2; doing so presupposes the root equality at the point where the carrier is instantiated.
not_claimed: No impossibility theorem for all Kato/Euler-system approaches.
No claim that BKS Theorem 1.3 is false or circular as a theorem.
